item.title: Tower Research hired a Millennium veteran for its MFT platform after the hedge fund hired its CTO
item.description:
Earlier this year, Millennium hired Alexandre Fournier </news/millennium-quietly-hired-the-cto-of-a-major-hft-firm-to-work-on-nanosecond-latency-architecture>, CTO of high-frequency trading </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm?_gl=1*1umudi4*_up*MQ..*_ga*MjEzNzI1NDI3NS4xNzkzNzI2NDA2*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3OTM3MjY0MDYkbzEkZzEkdDE3OTM3MjY1NDYkajYwJGwwJGg2NzkwMDI0NTc.> firm Tower Research, to work on low-latency technology. Turnabout is fair play, it seems, as Tower has now hired a veteran technologist of the hedge fund </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job>to aid its push into mid-frequency trading (MFT) strategies. </news/hft-jobs-medium-frequency-trading>
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Marvin Arteaga has joined Tower Research as its head of MFT strategies, based in New York. He was at Millennium for 12 years, predominantly serving as head of algo execution technologies. He spent seven years before that working in algo development at Bank of America. Curiously, Arteaga worked remotely in his last year at Millennium in the seemingly less senior role of 'liquidity provision technology manager.' His new role with Tower is hybrid.
MFT strategies involve holding positions for minutes to days, as opposed to HFT strategies where positions can be held for microseconds or less. Tower has been building out its MFT capabilities for years, much like other major players including Jane Street and Hudson River Trading. Iain Dunning, head of AI at Hudson River Trading, famously said last year that "all the latency has been arbitraged for the most part." MFT strategies are more likely to involve machine learning, which the major firms have been investing billions into <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-27/ai-talent-war-has-quant-firms-racing-to-fund-phds-build-labs>as they build out their compute stacks. </news/quant-trading-gpus>
It's not just technologists moving between Tower and Millennium. Wesley Chen, </news/tower-research-lost-a-top-credit-trader-to-hedge-fund-millennium-despite-fixed-income-push?_gl=1*1umudi4*_up*MQ..*_ga*MjEzNzI1NDI3NS4xNzkzNzI2NDA2*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3OTM3MjY0MDYkbzEkZzEkdDE3OTM3MjY1NDYkajYwJGwwJGg2NzkwMDI0NTc.>Tower's co-head of investment grade credit trading, joined Millennium as a portfolio manager in June.
Millennium declined to comment. Tower did not respond to a comment request.

item.title: Citadel Securities hired a new head of electronic equities sales from Goldman Sachs
item.description:
Ken Griffin appreciates the culture of Goldman Sachs </news/2023/10/citadel-goldman-sachs-114>, which may be part of the reason why Citadel Securities </news/2022/10/how-to-get-a-job-at-citadel>hired Goldman partner Jim Esposito to be president of the firm in 2024. He wasn't the first Goldman alum to join the market maker </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-an-electronic-trading-firm> and certainly isn't the last; the latest to join is a former Goldman MD taking a top sales role in its most established division.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Andrew Kalafarski has joined Citadel Securities as its 'head of equities electronic sales' according to his FINRA registration. He joined the firm a week ago, having spent the entirety of his 20-year career before that working at Goldman Sachs. He worked in the bank's electronic trading sales division, and was made MD in 2021 after being tipped for the promotion by our sources </news/2021/11/goldman-sachs-mds-2021>ahead of time.
Equities market making is Citadel Securities' pride and joy; the firm's website <https://www.citadelsecurities.com/what-we-do/equities/> states that it accounts for over 23% of total US equities execution. The team features several other Goldman alums in high-ranking positions including Joseph Anastasio, <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-11-06/citadel-securities-hires-sales-co-heads-for-block-equity-trades> co-head of high-touch equities sales trading, who spent 16 years at Goldman.
Alumni of the bank are also present in Citadel Securities' other rising divisions; one of its biggest hires of the year was Goldman partner Nikhil Choraria </news/nikhil-choraria-citadel-securities>, the firm's co-head of fixed income, who officially joined in September according to the FCA register. LinkedIn data suggests that Goldman Sachs is the most common former employer among the firm's external hires.

item.title: Citadel had a great October and has hired more people to calibrate PMs' performance
item.description:
In case you haven't noticed, hedge funds are having a hard time. </news/hedge-funds-hired-too-many-morons-and-other-unpopular-opinions-as-the-industry-pukes-p-ms>People are leaving; pods are closing </news/high-yield-hedge-fund-bloodbath>; Elliott Investment Management is warning of a market that might suddenly switch to FOGO (fear of getting obliterated).
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
In the circumstances, it should be easy to track portfolio managers </news/finance/portfolio-manager-job-hedge-fund-lifestyle> who are performing and portfolio managers who are not. The latter are the ones with the big losses who are being ejected from funds </news/london-s-macro-hedge-fund-pain-as-up-to-100-people-are-out-everyone-has-blown-up>in large numbers and who will be spending the winter wondering what to do next.
Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-03/major-hedge-funds-mostly-lose-in-nowhere-to-hide-october?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261103&utm_campaign=author_19458291>reports today that LMR (-0.8%), Dymon (-1.8%), NorthRock (-2.3%), Marshall Wace (-5.4% equity) and ExodusPoint (-2.4%) were among the funds down in October.
The FT <https://www.ft.com/content/fae029f1-f03e-4509-852e-396fa4863271?syn-25a6b1a6=1>says Millennium was down 2.3% in October. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-02/millennium-pulls-over-1-5-billion-from-two-external-hedge-funds?taid=6ae8fd5eec3fc200011e158f&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>reported yesterday that Millennium pulled $1.5bn of external investments from Axebrook and Troluce Capital after losses at both firms.
Citadel, by comparison, was up 1.7% in October according to the FT. As we observed last week </news/macro-hedge-fund-leavers>, a handful of people have left Citadel's London business for reasons that are not clear. Some left in September before the tribulations of the last month. Citadel declined to comment.
In a trend that is only indirectly related to improved performance, Citadel is among the funds that appear to be taking a more scientific approach to appraising staff. Citadel's large people analytics team is run by Davis Carlin, a former McKinsey & Co partner who joined in 2024. In January, Citadel hired Keith McNulty, </news/hedge-fund-citadel-hired-a-ph-d-talent-scientist-from-mc-kinsey>also from McKinsey, as head of assessments. In September, it hired people analytics specialist Kevin Navikas to cover the fixed income business in New York.
After their strong October, Citadel PMs may expect to be paid. But Richard Averill, founder of Waterline Economics, which provides compensation analytics for hedge funds, says it's no longer that simple. "Funds now try to take everything into account," says Averill. "It's not just about PnL but the costs involved, including brokerage, market data charges and team and office costs."
PnL made in an expensive way with heavy prime brokerage fees is less valuable than PnL made cheaply, observes Averill. Banks learned a similar lesson in 2008; hedge funds may be learning it in 2026.

item.title: Citi's equities business might need some new hires
item.description:
When Citi reported its third quarter results </news/citi-m-a-bankers> last month, its revenues suggested that M&A bankers </news/get-a-job-in-ma> there have been having a hard time relative to rivals, and that its equities salespeople and traders aren't especially thriving either. Although Citi's equities trading revenues were up nearly 33% in the first nine months, this was the worst performance of 10 major banks (save SocGen </news/socgen-fixed-income>). In the third quarter, Citi's equities sales and trading revenues rose only 14%; Goldman's were up 72%.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
What went wrong? It's not entirely clear. Citi said equities revenue growth was offset by a decline in derivatives revenues. Citi was the only major bank that said its Q3 equity derivatives sales and trading revenues fell year-on-year, although Wells Fargo said the quarter was tougher.
Speaking during the investor call, Citi CEO Jane Fraser said Citi was "late to invest in equities” and is trying to catch up. - "What we are systematically doing is scaling our equities business, primarily by committing the resources to grow the prime balances, making the necessary investments in technology,” Fraser declared. "So you’ll see us steadily investing in execution.”
The implication is that Citi will be hiring some new people in equities. This might be a good thing, as various people have left in recent months. "There is a hole that needs filling," suggests one trader at a rival firm.
The most recent departure is Stefan Herrenknecht, a pan-European sales trader whose gone to Bank of America after nearly 29 years. Previous exits include: Ross Taylor </news/ross-taylor-citi>, head of emerging markets sales trading, Ross Whittaker </news/another-electronic-equities-md-exited-citi>, an MD working on electronic sales trading in Hong Kong; Gabriel H. Tucci </news/citi-s-global-head-of-equities-execution-quants-is-leaving-a-london-md-is-off-the-desk>, global head of the equities execution quant team in New York; Jamie Miller, the co-head of EMEA electronic execution; and Anissa Dhouibi, </news/one-of-citi-s-top-equities-quants-resigned-maybe-her-team-will-follow> Citi's former global head of equities quantitative analysis, who's now at Millennium. </news/anissa-dhouibi-millennium>Dhouibi role was filled by London-based Holmi Atig in July.
Fater Belbachir, Citi's global head of equities trading, previously spent 15 years in equity derivatives trading at JPMorgan. Following the last quarter, he may want to hire some new equity derivatives traders too.
Citi declined to comment.

item.title: PJT probably won't pay its "outstanding people" $1m this year, after all
item.description:
As far as boutique investment banks </news/boutique-investment-banks> go, pay is good, and has always been good. Evercore is on track </news/evercore-q3-2026> to pay $1.2m per head in 2026, for example, up from $829k in 2024 and $973k in 2025. Pay at PJT Partners has been even better historically – so surely it’s paying even better, right? Right?
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/signup>✍️
Not right. PJT Partners did not have a great Q3, with revenue down by 14% in the quarter compared to Q3 of 2025. The first nine months of 2026 were still up on the first nine of 2025, however.
As such, compensation was down in the third quarter. Based on how much has been paid so far to the firm’s employees, pay per head for the year should come out to a rather measly $950k. The total compensation figure is still up on 2025 in the first nine months of the year, but not massively – and if 2026’s Q4 compensation bill simply matches 2025’s, then pay will have decreased to $929k. It needs a very strong end to the year to reach the coveted (by someone) $1m figure.
The firm has added headcount in the meantime. There are now 1,314 people employed at the boutique, up from 1,224 at the start of the year, 1,229 at the three-month-mark, and 1,234 at the six-month-mark. That increase probably has something to do with the huge number of internship applications </news/pjt-q2-2026> PJT received this year, some of which likely became members of its graduate program.
One place where headcount has certainly declined, however, is the number of dealmakers that the firm employs. Its partner headcount rose from 133 at the start of the year to 141 at the end of Q1 to 142 at the end of Q2. It’s now just 140.
Luckily for founder & CEO Paul Taubman, people still like working for him. “Outstanding people with strong intellectual curiosity, passion and empathy,” one of the bank’s employees said in PJT’s investor presentation. It’s also what they said at the start of the year </news/pjt-q4-2025>, so take that as you will – although they did also mention “humor” then.
Taubman himself also repeated, in his commentary on the Q3 results, a phrase he used earlier this year: “we remain highly confident in our future growth prospects.” Perhaps consistency in opinion is part of the firm’s values.

item.title: The top paying tech jobs in London: Jane Street, Citadel, Meta and More
item.description:
There are good paying technology jobs </news/how-to-get-a-technology-job-bank> in London and there are great paying ones. Above all that, there are Citadel, </news/2022/10/how-to-get-a-job-at-citadel> Jane Street </news/how-to-get-a-job-at-jane-street> and Meta </news/working-hours-banking-vs-tech>. A compensation heatmap <https://www.levels.fyi/heatmap/europe/> provided by benchmarking platform Levels.fyi says that these three companies are the top paying employers for software engineering jobs in London, but how much more do they pay than the rest?
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
We've broken down average total compensation for those three companies based on available Levels.fyi data and compared it Levels' UK benchmarks as well as several notable employers across both banking </news/career-paths-technology-banking> and fintech </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-fintech>. Those other firms pay more than the average, but much less than the 90th percentile for London engineers, and (with the exception of Stripe), £100k less on average than the three highest paying companies.
London software engineers working for electronic trading firm Jane Street appear to be the most well-off. They reported average total compensation (TC) of £252k on average, whereas Meta and Citadel each reported closer to £225k. It had the smallest sample size of the three firms, however. These engineers may also feel underpaid compared to Jane Street's traders; the firm reported average compensation of ~£1.4m in 2025 </news/jane-street-pay> according to accounts filed with Companies House.
The way that compensation is distributed also varies across each firm. The tech/fintech firms all pay hefty amounts of stock as part of their TC; at Meta, stock comprises just under half of the total package. London-based fintech bank Revolut pays the least amount of stock among them, and the smallest amount in bonuses whereas Stripe pays the highest proportion of cash bonuses among them.
It's a different story in banks and trading firms. There, stock pay is largely non-existent, and bonuses are larger. At Citadel and Jane Street, bonuses are just over a third of total compensation, whereas banking tech bonuses comprise ~15% of total pay.
There are other firms out there which might pay you more. OpenAI is a relatively new entrant to the UK, and paid its total headcount an average of £2.3m last year </news/open-ai-outpaid-quant-trading-firms-in-london-last-year-offering-2m-per-head-including-stock>according to Companies House; the AI lab has just four datapoints on Levels.fyi for London software engineers, with total compensation averaging £432.6k

item.title: London credit traders lament tragic death of ex-Barclays colleague
item.description:
Senior credit traders in London are mourning the death of 44-year-old Adam Robinson, a former credit trader who died with his wife and two children, their nanny and two friends, in the Learjet that was flying from Austin Texas to the Bahamas on November 1st.
Robinson, who was American, worked in London for Barclays following the financial crisis after beginning his career at Lehman Brothers in NYC. He founded an email marketing company in 2012 and achieved an "eight figure exit" in 2021 according to his LinkedIn profile. He'd latterly been working on another technology-based marketing company and on APIs offering contact data to AI agents.
Many of the thousand plus people mourning Robinson on LinkedIn are fellow tech entrepreneurs, who describe him as a legend. "You built great products, mad respect," says one. Former Barclays London colleagues tell us they are shocked and saddened by his passing too. "He was just a good guy, well liked by everyone. I never heard a bad word said about him," one tells us.
Speaking on the ProfitLed podcast <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dtPmEAYSxpE>only last week, Robinson said he spent 10 years as a CDS trader and made millions of dollars in two consecutive years in his 20s. He moved to London after the financial crisis, but things had changed: "My boss thought Europe was going to come unwound... Sent a bunch of people over there. Everyone shorted everything. Nobody made money. He gave everyone donuts. Zero zero bonuses."
Robinson was fired and moved back to live with a girlfriend in New York, but she broke up with him. He said he then had an "indescribably horrible" identity crisis. "[I’d] never experienced depression before in my life... I remember this one girl telling me, ‘Just make it through today.’ And I was like, ‘I don’t know how.’ Not that I was suicidal, it was just so painful to experience that loss of identity.”
At that point, Robinson told the podcast that he decided to leave trading and to build companies outside of financial services. He said that people who leave finance "have an enormous amount of confidence," but that it's very often misplaced. "When your value system has been for 10 years [that] your value is the money that you make, and you make a lot of money, you’re like, ‘Well, I can just do anything.’ And that’s probably true, but it’s probably true over a decade, and you think it’s true over six months."
Had he not made millions early in his career, Robinson said he may have stayed in trading. But he also said that the industry can be a trap. "You’re always looking at your boss and then your boss’s boss and trying to extrapolate: ‘Wow, if I just hang around, I’m going to have that cool apartment and buy that Hamptons house.’ That’s what the whole thing is.”
Another of Robinson's former trading colleagues tells us: "He was a great guy who achieved incredible success after Wall Street, but really cared about sharing how he did it and showing other people how they could do it too." The last part is "really unusual," he added.
RIP.

item.title: Morning Coffee: The most impressive 30-year-old hedge fund manager in New York is a Cambridge graduate. No vibe coding at Goldman Sachs
item.description:
Business Insider <https://www.businessinsider.com/wall-street-rising-stars-finance-leaders-2026-11?utm_source=Iterable&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=Business%20Insider%20Today%20%E2%80%94%20Nov%202%202026> has released a list of Rising Stars of Wall Street. It does not contain the now infamous figure of 24-year-old Leopold Aschenbrenner </news/leopold-aschenbrenner-hedge-fund-24>, high-cheeked founder of Situational Awareness, the hedge fund that lost $35bn in July. It does contain at least five young portfolio managers, and at least eight young bankers busy financing the AI infrastructure boom.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
The youngest and most impressive portfolio manager listed is Ben Atlas, the mere 30-year-old ex-Barclays rates trader in London who's now CIO of his own $1bn pod at ExodusPoint in New York.
Business Insider is short on details for Atlas, who didn't provide a photo or divulge how he spends weekends. Noted, instead, are the facts that Atlas grew up in California and went to Cambridge University in the UK to study philosophy before staying on in London after he graduated in 2017. He returned to the US in 2020 to work for DRW in New York.
Atlas worked for BlueCrest before ExodusPoint. Business Insider says he made more than $50m in profits for Mike Platt during his final year there, aged only 29. BlueCrest's pay structure </news/bluecrest> implies Atlas may have kept $15m of this for himself.
Atlas has become something of a legend among young London traders, who tell us he's one of a few 20-something portfolio managers to have made huge amounts of money in the past few years. Atlas is rumoured to have married a Deutsche Bank trader and to have had a large wedding attended by an unknown pop star, but this is not confirmed.
Others on the Business Insider list include: 27-year-old Theo Saarinen at Bridgewater, who is chief AI researcher there; 32-year-old Goldman Sachs MD Mike Washington, who works in high touch sales trading; and 31-year-old Sahil Singhal Balyasny Asset Management who now works for Balyasny but who says he was one of the youngest PMs at Citadel, aged only around 22.
Women on the list seem more likely to be financing data centres. 32-year-old Kate Casey is a director in KKR's infrastructure group who alludes to herself as working on the "data centre support team." Casey is married to a man whose family run a vineyard. 33-year-old Cody Kiechle (a man on the list) is also financing data centres at Bank of America, but grew up driving tractors on a farm.
Separately bankers and traders at Goldman Sachs no longer have the freedom to create their own tools using AI.
Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-02/goldman-restricts-traders-and-bankers-from-using-some-ai-tools?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261102&utm_campaign=author_21835441 > reports that the firm has put a stop to such vibe-coding and that now only actual developers and strats at Goldman can use AI coding tools themselves.
The change is reportedly the result of productivity and risk-related concerns and is possibly the result of traders and bankers trying to get developers to improve their creations. It is not entirely popular. Individuals at Goldman had reportedly created their own tools to monitor client trading flows, model market changes and positions, and create content.
Meanwhile...
Elliott Investment Management says times are hard. “So many factors have lined up to cause this great boom that it might take disruption in only one or two of them to shift this momentum into reverse, leading to a cascading, self-reinforcing unwind of this bull market and an abrupt change from FOMO to FOGO (fear of getting obliterated).” (WSJ) <https://www.wsj.com/finance/investing/hedge-fund-elliott-warns-of-fogo-fear-of-getting-obliterated-in-the-market-a2cc7027?mod=panda_wsj_author_alert>
Most hedge funds are levered six times. Multistrats are levered an average of eight to 14 times and many are holding the same assets. "A shock affecting these managers together would meet high leverage, overlapping positions.” (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-02/multistrat-giants-crowd-into-same-trades-raising-odds-of-a-rout?taid=6ae8b39fec3fc200014a1569&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
Millennium is redeeming $1.5bn from external funds Troluce Capital Advisors and Axebrook Capital after they made losses. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-02/millennium-pulls-over-1-5-billion-from-two-external-hedge-funds?taid=6ae8fd5eec3fc200011e158f&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
Banks are back to hiring from a few universities. In the UK, these include The London School of Economics, Imperial College London, University College London, the University of Oxford and University of Cambridge. (Financial News) <https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/working-class-students-struggle-to-secure-banking-internships-8912b5ce>
Boutique bank Qatalyst Partners was the lead financial adviser to chip giant Marvell Technology on its $102.6 billion takeover of laser supplier Lumentum Holdings. This is three times larger than Qatalyst's previous largest deal. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-02/qatalyst-notches-its-biggest-deal-with-rare-buyside-m-a-role?taid=6ae8fe89aa388300014de013&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
HM Revenue & Customs is investigating whether some partners at Boston Consulting should be employees for tax purposes. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/7b5d0e4f-6c66-433e-84a7-558bf6bb3026?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
CFA Institute is launching a new Responsible AI in Investment Research course. It will be a practical skills module and will focus on use of the technology while preserving rigour, independent judgement, verification, ethical responsibility and accountability. All the adjectives. (Financial News) <https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/cfa-institute-shifts-towards-hands-on-skills-and-ai-training-cfe56f22?mod=homepage>
How one trader turned divorce counsellor </news/divorce-banking-trading> persuades his male clients to consider different types of women: "If you were always putting on the same trade and it was going wrong each time, what would you do?” (The Times) <https://www.thetimes.com/life-style/sex-relationships/article/divorce-coach-city-men-vms08lqbh>
If you want to lock down a sperm donor so that no one else gets the sperm, it will cost you at least $80k. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2026-11-02/ivf-parents-are-paying-80-000-for-exclusive-rights-to-donor-sperm?taid=c083c703-1614-4df3-ac57-c7152b003c37&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>
The more you use AI, the longer you work. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2026-11-02/ai-is-making-employees-work-longer-days-new-data-shows?taid=6ae8744181a2370001fe3237&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>

item.title: Most "hardcore" 25-year-old in finance reveals his identity, has no regrets
item.description:
When Revolut CEO Nik Storonsky </news/nik-storonsky-revolut>participated in a podcast <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hT_MAAwFLIc&t=2018s> last month, he revealed his dislike for venture capitalists on the grounds that they are often not "operators who know how to do things", but board level meddlers.
Evidencing this, Storonsky said that at one point in Revolut's past, a VC who'd invested in the company tried to make him fire his best person. The VC said the person was too "hardcore," said Storonsky. He said he refused to oblige the VC, kept his best person on and instead removed VCs from the board at each investment round.
Storonsky didn't reveal who his hardcore operator was, but the person has since outed themselves. It was, unsurprisingly, Alan Chang. </news/alan-chang-revolut-fuse>
Chang joined Revolut straight out of Imperial aged 21. He left again as a multi-multi-millionaire aged 28. During his time at Revolut Chang was everything from head of operations, to head of customer services, to chief revenue officer. Chang now runs Fuse Energy, a UK-based renewable energy supplier. When we spoke to Chang a year ago, he said he was still working 80-90 hours a week.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Writing on LinkedIn, Chang said he learned about the VC's effort to fire him in 2020 when the drunken VC admitted it during the Revolut Series D closing dinner. "He apologised. Said he was wrong once he saw what I could do," said Chang. "Nik is 100% right. Most investors can't be trusted with any power over the company. They should cheer from the sidelines and count their returns."
Burned from this experience, Chang said he's written "constitutional docs" at Fuse which specifically say VCs can't fire him. This is probably wise, given that some Fuse employees have reportedly <https://observer.co.uk/news/business/article/they-milk-them-to-the-max-fuse-energy-accused-of-mistreating-staff> complained of a harsh working environment there too.
Chang is not about cosy jobs, though. Chang is about building companies and making a lot of money from stock. At Revolut, he said he asked to be paid minimum wage and took the rest as shares. He says this was a good decision given that his Revolut shares are now worth $10m+.
However Chang - who didn't respond to a request to comment for this article - also says that he and his co-founder Charles Orr have invested "nearly everything we had" in Fuse. If the company fails, Chang says they will both be "fcked". Presumably this encourages more hardcore working practices than ever.

item.title: Citi hired Cocks from Barclays to co-head its healthcare ECM business
item.description:
It's a good time to join Citi's equity capital markets (ECM) business. </news/citi-m-a-bankers> Its global market share has grown to 6.3%, up from 4.6% last year, and its share in North America is the highest it has been since 2021. There's still room to grow, though, and the bank has made a senior hire from Barclays to facilitate that.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Dan Cocks has joined Citi has co-head of healthcare ECM </news/skills-needed-capital-markets> according to his LinkedIn. FINRA <https://brokercheck.finra.org/individual/summary/5904801>shows him joining the bank in New York as of Wednesday last week. Before that, he was an MD at Barclays focused on biotech ECM. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2023-07-18/barclays-hires-dan-cocks-from-goldman-sachs-for-biotech-ecm> reported at the time that he joined the British Bank from Goldman Sachs, where he worked as an MD in ECM syndicate operations.
Cocks might be running the business with Jennifer Sheng, a Greenwich Connecticut-based MD who has worked for Citi since 2019. She was named co-head of North American healthcare ECM last year <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2025-03-11/citigroup-taps-chris-chung-to-run-north-america-ecm-syndicate>, but touts a non-regional title in a more recent bio <https://bigs.bio.org/speakers/jennifer-sheng> for an upcoming conference appearance. Citi declined to comment.
Healthcare, and biotech in particular, is a lucrative area of ECM today. The Wall Street Journal <https://www.wsj.com/pro/venture-capital/biotech-ipos-charge-ahead-as-tech-deals-stall-75d3c65c>reported last month that there had been 23 biotech IPOs </news/spacex-ipo-2nd-tier-bank> in the first three quarters of 2026, compared to eight IPOs in the entirety of last year.

item.title: The finance professionals most afraid of AI are 28-year-old credit trading VPs in Hong Kong
item.description:
Are you afraid of AI taking your job? Join the club. We recently conducted a survey on AI in finance, asking roughly 2,500 people whether they were afraid of being replaced by AI. </news/how-to-get-a-banking-ai-job>29% of professional respondents said they were, but some groups were much more afraid than others.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
We’ve looked in depth at the identities of respondents to this question, including their age, location and sector to see who, in theory, is the group most afraid of AI.
Most concerned: 28-year-old credit trading VPs in Hong Kong
APAC had the highest percentage of professional respondents who said they were either ‘concerned’ or ‘very concerned’ about being replaced by AI, with 43% responding with one of the two answers. Among countries with 30+ respondents, Hong Kong </news/hong-kong-banking-jobs-vs-new-york> was the most negative, with more than 40% expressing their concern.
Sales and trading, </news/sales-and-trading-ai> meanwhile, was the most fearful sector in finance. Credit sales and trading is particularly afraid, with 48% of respondents actively employed in the space saying they’re concerned. It’s a space that is increasingly exposed to electronification, and the big cumbersome banks that have dominated the market are also facing competition from market makers and prop trading firms that run with significantly smaller headcounts. </news/credit-trading>
The other factors were negligible. Fear over AI is pretty evenly split between men and women, marginally tipping towards the latter, whereas 26-30-year-olds as a group were just 1% more fearful than 18-25-year-olds.
One respondent matched this description entirely, except for the fact that she was based in Singapore. She said that she’s “not really sure how to be prepared” for the incoming storm of AI. She said that the technology can cover “basically all my tasks” and that she’s looking at options to change career before it’s too late.
It’s not just younger traders who are scared. A female Singaporean credit trading professional in her late 30s said that AI is “super scary” and that it will “eventually kill” her industry.
Interestingly, when looking only at who answered that they were ‘very concerned’ about AI, the hypothetical profile is similar, but different: a 26-year-old male Singaporean credit trading VP.
Least concerned: 50 year old Italian asset managers
Finance is a relationships-based industry, so it’s unsurprising that the group least afraid of being replaced is the group that has spent the most time building those relationships. Respondents aged 50+ were the most likely to say that they were ‘not concerned at all’ about being replaced by AI.
49% of respondents on the buy-side said they had no fear of AI, the highest of any sector. Asset managers and private equity professionals were particularly unperturbed.
Italy had the lowest rate of concern with AI among professionals; more than half of respondents had no fears. The next least afraid was the US at 46% of respondents.
It helps that older professionals are the people making the hiring decisions. One Italian hedge fund </news/how-hedge-funds-use-ai> PM said that AI will make things much easier for him in the future as there will be “no junior analysts needed.

item.title: Goldman Sachs' European head of government bond trading may have quietly retired
item.description:
Garry Naughton had a good run at Goldman Sachs, but now it is our understanding that he is going.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Neither Goldman nor Garry responded to a request to comment for this article, but sources suggested Garry is retiring.
Naughton was Goldman's European head of government bond trading. We last wrote about him when he joined Goldman from Deutsche Bank. That was 12 years ago.
Naughton is thought to have left Goldman of his own accord. At least one junior on the team is thought to have been less fortunate. </news/goldman-sachs-cut-some-jobs-last-week-it-s-that-time-of-year>
Goldman's London macro team has been through some changes. Many former stars are now at Citadel Securities, including Nikhil Choraria </news/nikhil-choraria-citadel-securities>, Nohshad Shah, Frank Flight and Ishaan Sethi (via Marshall Wace).
Goldman said its rates trading business was weak in the third quarter. It was also weak in the first quarter. </news/maybe-goldman-sachs-and-nordea-should-leave-risky-rates-trading-to-citadel-securities>It's thought to be hiring.

item.title: The satirical memoirs of an MD in an investment bank: The burden of the corporate card
item.description:
There is a small black rectangle in my wallet that has shaped my adult life more than my education, my marriage or, if I am honest, my children.
It is the corporate Amex.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
People assume the card is a privilege. Junior staff </news/banks-weird-hierarchies-analysts-associates-vps-mds>look at it the way a Labrador looks at a sausage. What they do not see is the weight of it. Every time I place that card on a white tablecloth, I am making a decision on behalf of the shareholders, the clients and, in a sense, the entire British financial services sector. It is not a card. It is a responsibility with a contactless function.
In March we went to Lisbon to pitch for a logistics group's treasury business. Rahul had spent six weeks building the pitch. Priya came because she is the only person in the building who can answer questions on settlement timelines without looking them up.
We flew out on a Tuesday. I flew business, which is firm policy for anyone at Managing Director level on flights over two hours. Lisbon is two hours and forty minutes, which I have always felt is exactly the right length for a policy to kick in.
Before the flight I spent an hour in the lounge. Through the glass I could see Rahul and Priya at the gate, sitting on the floor by a plug socket, sharing one laptop. I raised my glass to them. Rahul, after a moment, raised a paper cup of coffee back, which I thought showed good team spirit.
That evening, after the meeting, I took the chairman and his daughter, the CFO, to dinner. I did not invite Rahul or Priya, because four is a better number for intimacy and five would have looked like a delegation. They ate at a café near the hotel. I know this because Priya's receipt came through the next morning: eleven euros, soup and bread.
The bill at our dinner came to just under two thousand four hundred euros. I placed the card on the tablecloth with, I like to think, a certain calm.
At nine the following evening, the CFO emailed to say they would move their business to us. Her email was three sentences long. The first said that her father had liked me, which was worth something. The second said that Rahul's proposal and Priya's settlement procedure were worth more. The third said that together they had made the decision easy.
I read the first sentence several times. I think it is the nicest thing a client has ever written to me.
Later that month, I noticed a small line on Priya's expense report, which I approve. It was eleven euros for soup and bread in Lisbon. There was a note from Finance asking her to confirm it was within the per diem, as the receipt was slightly faded.
I approved it straight away. I am not a monster.
Photo: Unsplash
This is an extract from Great Work, Richard, available on Amazon in Kindle and paperback. <https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B0HL59CH2K> The author has over 10 years' experience in investment banking. Richard Ashworth-Hale is a pseudonym

item.title: Barclays hired a rates trader known as G-Unit and people are excited
item.description:
These are tough times and they are especially tough times in macro </news/london-s-macro-hedge-fund-pain-as-up-to-100-people-are-out-everyone-has-blown-up> at Barclays, where the third quarter was so feeble </news/barclays-fixed-income-traders-are-getting-bigger-bonuses-at-just-the-wrong-time>that Barclays' CEO C.S. Venkatakrishnan said the D-word ("disappointing") and that the bank is "giving this attention". Some of this attention seems to involve hiring new people.
We suggested earlier that Barclays might hire Zoeb Sachee, </news/citi-s-big-euro-rates-trader-left-what-if-he-goes-to-barclays> who has been newly unleashed from Citi. In fact, Barclays has hired Graham Bates, who was last seen at Capula.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Barclays isn't commenting but multiple sources say Bates joined the bank. The FCA Register says Bates' middle name is Paul and that he left Capula in July 2024 after four years there. He previously spent over a decade at JPMorgan.
Bates has presumably decided that now is not an opportune time to go to a macro hedge fund.
Bates is sometimes referred to as G-Unit in reflection of his propensity for risk-taking. It's thought he's head of euro swaps trading at Barclays. Bates will have the opportunity to work with Puni Raja, </news/punitha-raja-barclays> Barclays' star real money rates sales guy. He will also have the opportunity to work with Tanya Kohli, Barclays' UK head of pensions and insurance rates sales, with whom he previously worked at JPMorgan.
Barclays is accumulating traders from hedge funds Last month it rehired Julien Ercole </news/julien-ercole-barclays>, its former head of peripheral European government bond trading from Point72. It also hired Mark Wade </news/barclays-hired-the-whale-from-nomura>, a STIR trader from Nomura.
Barclays still has a vacancy for a head of European rates trading after Hamza Houmaddy </news/barclays-s-head-of-european-rates-trading-is-leaving> left a few weeks ago.

item.title: Goldman Sachs cut some jobs last week. It's that time of year
item.description:
Goldman Sachs didn't discuss job cuts </news/only-goldman-sachs-jp-morgan-morgan-stanley-and-nomura-didn-t-mention-cost-cuts-in-q4>when it reported its third quarter results. This does not mean that Goldman Sachs is not cutting jobs.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Multiple sources tell us that Goldman cut some jobs last week. It's not clear how many jobs were cut, but it's standard for the firm to cut 3-4% of staff </news/goldman-sachs-might-be-warming-up-for-some-more-job-cuts-soon>in September as part of its "strategic resource assessment" (SRA). Unconfirmed reports suggest 5%+ of some teams disappeared.
Goldman Sachs didn't comment on the cuts. Insiders suggest they encompassed areas including sales and trading </news/how-do-you-get-a-job-in-sales-and-trading-in-a-bank> and technology. Speaking off the record, one senior technologist told us "anyone not involved in cloud" had been vulnerable to the cuts and that even AI teams had been trimmed.
Goldman ended Q3 with 47,500 staff. This was 1,300 more than at the end of Q2 (+3%), but 800 fewer than a year earlier (-2%).
The firm's Q3 earnings release attributed the 1,300 new people added to “the timing of campus hires.” If more than 1,3000 new analysts and associates joined, then Goldman also cut people in Q3. Business Insider <https://www.businessinsider.com/goldman-sachs-layoffs-cuts-underperformers-sra-spring-summer-2026-3>said in March that Goldman was adopting a new approach of cutting people throughout the year.

item.title: Barclays hired Standard Chartered's former global head of cloud and moved him to London
item.description:
Barclays is in the process of cutting thousands of jobs </news/barclays-ai-job-cuts> with the help of AI. </news/how-to-get-a-banking-ai-job> To do this, it needs senior technologists to build out the architecture; Barclays has hired a new tech MD who spent the last 12 years working in Singapore across both banks and technology firms to do just that.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Carl Bachman Kharazmi joined Barclays late last month as group head of engineering and architecture, based in London. He was most recently a global director of communication governance startup LeapXpert, which raised $180m in growth funding <https://ffnews.com/news/leapxpert-secures-180m-growth-round-to-scale-governed-ai-communications-platform> shortly after he joined.
Before that, Kharazmi was head of platform engineering for Singaporean exchange group SGX for a year. He also spent three years at Standard Chartered, where he was global head of cloud, and was a cloud engineering </news/cloud-engineer-job-security-finance>lead for Google for over three years.
Barclays staff may welcome a technology specialist. We reported last week that a letter from alleged Barclays insiders said that chief AI officer Anita Tanna, who made her name in equity sales, lacked "deep domain expertise" </news/barclays-head-of-ai> in computer science.
Barclays isn't the only bank cutting heads. Standard Chartered, Kharazmi's old haunt, announced plans to cut 7,000 jobs in May, focusing on "lower-value human capital." </news/lower-value-human-capital> Citi has quietly been making cuts across the middle and back office this year </news/citi-s-2026-layoffs-have-been-more-frequent-and-widespread-than-we-thought>; last month, it hired Google engineering director Sebastian Gnagnarella as head of its 'agent factory' who might help expedite that process.

item.title: Citi's big euro rates trader left. What if he goes to Barclays?
item.description:
Zoeb Sachee left Citi. Late last Friday, while everyone else was dressed as a ghoul, Sachee wrote on LinkedIn that it is "time for his next chapter."
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Everyone is wondering which chapter that will be.
Sachee, who was based in Paris, spent 36 years at Citi, having joined in 1990. Since 2009, he's been head of rates trading in various forms. His departure is a big deal.
We have not spoken to Sachee, who said he left with "enormous gratitude and great pride" and that his "enthusiasm for markets, building businesses and leading teams is as strong as ever."
The implication is that he is not retiring and that he either wants or already has a new job.
Some are wondering whether his new job might be at Barclays. Hamza Houmaddy, </news/barclays-s-head-of-european-rates-trading-is-leaving> the head of European rates trading at Barclays unexpectedly resigned a few weeks ago. Julien Ercole, </news/julien-ercole-barclays> a robust Italian risk taker has since joined Barclays, but maybe there's space for Sachee too?

item.title: Morning Coffee: Hedge funds' high yield bloodbath - "Everyone is scared." Jeopardy of the sudden meeting in your diary
item.description:
As we reported </news/european-high-yield> nearly two weeks ago, hedge funds </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job> with high yield investments have been having a hard time. The extent of this is now becoming clear.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
The Financial Times <https://www.ft.com/content/fdc9a85d-d2c4-465f-99ca-609d68b6d443?syn-25a6b1a6=1>has been talking to some high yield investors who have declared that things are not going so well. “It’s a complete bloodbath,” says one portfolio manager at a large US hedge fund. “Everyone is scared of being in the next blow-up.” Pods at multistrategy hedge funds </news/multistrategy-hedge-funds-hiring> that are invested in high yield assets are being forced to close, says the FT. "Being flat is the new up."
The bloodbath in high yield follows the bloodbath in macro. </news/london-s-macro-hedge-fund-pain-as-up-to-100-people-are-out-everyone-has-blown-up>There is potential too for a bloodbath in equities as the FT <https://www.ft.com/content/3ba953ae-84bb-4de4-959e-baec3e908fb3?syn-25a6b1a6=1> says the large positions that hedge funds built in the Magnificent 7 tech stocks are being 'violently unwound.' Charlie McElligott, Nomura's big-bearded cross-asset strategist, observes that this is all helpfully happening just as 2026 hedge fund bonuses are under consideration.
It's a bad time, then, not least because when we were last speaking to a veteran of high yield credit investing, he suggested that the entire asset class in Europe had become uninvestable. This is the result of "drop down strategies" facilitated by an eruption of weak covenants allowing companies to move assets into new subsidiaries, leaving bonds secured against far less collateral.
The founder of one fund confirmed to the FT that drop down strategies are causing big problems. " We are now seeing a new reality — where [private equity owners] are deeply out of the money on their original investment and documentation is loose [leaving lenders exposed to assets being shifted], opening up a wider range of outcomes for creditors,” he explained.
As investors rush to escape their high yield investments, the FT notes that yields on the lowest rated CCC bonds are climbing rapidly. Investors holding large quantities of these bonds have been unable to sell out of their positions. Now they have large losses.
"It's a broken market," the veteran credit PM told us a few weeks ago. "Assets are being destabilized and you see the covenants that have been applied to everything are worthless. I wouldn't go back to a fund now."
Separately, beware the meeting unexpectedly inserted in your diary by HR.
Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-31/how-weil-gotshal-collapsed-law-firm-crashed-to-a-close-in-days?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261031&utm_campaign=author_22980254> reports that a meeting was inserted for staff at Weil Gotshal Manages. They received a sudden Zoom meeting announcement on 3.30pm on Wednesday and were told that the management of the law firm was recommending it be wound down. Juniors are getting 90 days pay; many only joined the week before, back when Weil Gotshal was still boasting </news/weil-gotshal-made-some-unfortunate-posts-about-being-a-great-place-to-work>about being a great place to work.
Meanwhile...
Credit hedge fund Hamza Lemssouguer's Arini Capital Management has been looking to sell some of its most liquid and performing assets as a way to manage its portfolio and raise cash. Pacific Investment Management Co. and Oaktree Capital Management might be interested in buying the debt of Sabre Corp, for example. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-30/arini-gets-bids-on-junk-debt-from-pimco-oaktree-as-losses-mount?utm_source=website&utm_medium=share&utm_campaign=twitter>
Proceeds from some of the trades went to meet margin requirements tied to investment in credit default swap indexes and other trades, people familiar with the matter said. (WSJ) <https://www.wsj.com/finance/investing/hedge-fund-arini-offloads-800-million-in-debt-as-losses-deepen-2d24626c?st=gij2zf&reflink=article_copyURL_share>
“The major tech names are entering a no man’s land where they become uninvestable. When heavyweights like SoftBank halve in value over a few months, it is neither a buy nor a sell. Investors will want to simply keep out of the way.” (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/3ba953ae-84bb-4de4-959e-baec3e908fb3?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Intel shares are still nearly double where they were a year ago. (Polemic Paine <https://polemicpaine.substack.com/p/the-stool-the-sheds-and-the-thirty?utm_source=substack&publication_id=7260679&post_id=222784324&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=qrn8&triedRedirect=true>)
The billion-dollar question is can Millennium deploy another $22 billion without structurally eroding their returns. (Rupak Ghose) <https://rupakghose.substack.com/p/is-the-hedge-fund-industry-too-large?utm_source=post-email-title&publication_id=1898843&post_id=222783200&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=k3np9&triedRedirect=true&utm_medium=email>
Weil Gotshal Manges was known by employees as “We’re Gonna Match” when lawyers fielded competing offers. It was among the most profitable law firms with profits per equity partner over $5m. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-31/how-weil-gotshal-collapsed-law-firm-crashed-to-a-close-in-days?utm_medium=email&utm_source=author_alert&utm_term=261031&utm_campaign=author_22980254>
Partners from a generation ago have a Weil pension that is fully funded. Weil lawyers hired in recent years do not have a defined retirement benefit plan. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/8332fa3f-2a4a-41ca-8836-44d41d32fe8a?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Eddie Manheimer from Morgan Stanley is joining Bank of America as head of global power and utilities investment banking. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-30/bofa-hires-senior-power-banker-manheimer-from-morgan-stanley>
The Italian government has got a draft budget proposing that wealthy residents who leave the country from 2027 will have to pay a 26% tax on unrealised gains on assets worth over €800k. (IMI) <https://www.imidaily.com/europe/italy-budget-bill-proposes-26-exit-tax-on-residents-leaving-with-e800000-or-more/>
Greece is offering a €100,000 annual flat tax on foreign-sourced income and 50 per cent exemption on Greek-source employment or business income. It's also cut the tax rate on carried interest to 5%. Conditions apply. (FT) <https://www.ft.com/content/89dffe1c-d1bf-4f63-a281-0aecf69796bd?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
Lloyds has got a round of voluntary redundancies. (The Times) <https://www.thetimes.com/business/companies-markets/article/lloyds-launches-redundancy-round-as-rivals-make-sweeping-job-cuts-r5sqdb56z>
Chloe Moffat, 26, was told in May 2025 by managers at the Treasury that they had received allegations she had shared sensitive confidential information. She denied this and the next day she took her own life. A coroner found that holding “informal fact-finding” meetings with employees accused of misconduct posed a risk of future deaths. (The Times) <https://www.thetimes.com/article/62b83bc2-e7b9-4cba-83aa-00b3a6f29f57?shareToken=53899bdd4c00eb538e05faf2deb06d8b>
HSBC has already got an AI institute in Singapore. Now it will have one in Hong Kong too. (Reuters) <https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/hsbc-open-hong-kong-ai-institute-following-singapore-launch-2026-11-02/>
No one wants to hire non-Mandarin speaking Europeans in Hong Kong now. One European expatriate sent out over 200 job applications and has coffee meetings with contacts, hiring managers and companies every day; he still doesn't have a job. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2026-10-29/hong-kong-expats-struggle-to-find-jobs-without-speaking-mandarin-cantonese?utm_source=whatsapp&utm_medium=social&utm_content=business>

item.title: The Wilderness Diaries, Episode 4: Negapositivity
item.description:
My brother keeps telling me to take the positive out of the negative: my former employer was simply not meant to be, and my health is in great shape, which is what matters most.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
I agree, but I often object. Perhaps I am a strange creature, but I need to work to stay healthy. That is how I am wired.
So, let us stay positive. I was determined to get back on my feet as soon as possible. No time off, whatever those around me suggested. “Straight back in” became my daily motto.
Within two weeks of the redundancy, I sent out CV </news/the-absolutely-perfect-investment-banking-cv> 1.0. Zero answers. Doubts began to settle in. Again.
Remain positive, I told myself. Could it be the CV? With the help of a trusted ex-colleague, now a recruiter, I revamped it. CV 2.0 went out and, bingo: two requests for a call within four weeks. High positivity.
The famous corporate social network platform is full of daily positive quotes from guys who know exactly how to close a deal. And if you cannot, you are just a muppet.
Then I learnt something new. These calls are known as screenings. They check your credentials and salary expectations, and nothing more. “I will pass your CV to the hiring manager.”
I refreshed my inbox. Then refreshed it again. Then came a deafening silence. Remain positive. I followed up a few days later. No reply.
Eventually, a friendly HR officer called. “I am sorry for the delay. The hiring manager has decided not to pursue your application, as other candidates are better aligned with the role.” Fair enough.
Then came the never-ending PR exercise, which still annoys me to this day: “I will keep your CV in mind. Is that fine with you?” Six months on, I am still waiting for one of those calls.
Worse, a few weeks afterwards I spotted a similar role, more closely aligned with my skills, on an online financial recruitment site and contacted the same person. He ghosted me.
Everyone tells me not to worry, that something will turn up soon. Nothing has.
I have been approved for Jobseeker’s Allowance. My compulsory meeting is scheduled for the following week. 9.00 am sharp, I am told.
Click here for Episode 1. </news/losing-your-job-in-banking>

item.title: One of Nomura's top Singapore prop traders resigned
item.description:
Having been blown away in the aftermath of financial crisis, proprietary (prop) traders are a thing of the past at most banks in most jurisdictions. Most banks want their traders hedging and market making instead.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Nomura is not most banks. It still employs people to take proprietary risk and now one of them is not there. Pawan Bhargava in Singapore has resigned.
Nomura didn't respond to a request to comment for this article and nor did Bhargava himself. We have it on good authority, though, that Bhargava left this week to the surprise of colleagues.
It's not clear where he's going next.
Bhargava joined Nomura in 2022 after 18 years as a STIRT trader at Credit Suisse where he was latterly head of G10 FX fowards trading. </news/2022/11/credit-suisse-traders-leaving>

item.title: Weil Gotshal made some unfortunate posts about being a great place to work
item.description:
If you're a student embarking upon a legal career in 2026 and you see social media posts about a law firm running a mentoring panel promising "deep commitment to developing the next generation of outstanding lawyers," you might feel intrigued. If that same law firm announces plans for its own dissolution 24 hours later and then fires <https://www.ft.com/content/98dfc71b-19eb-4194-8c6a-bb6d9b463074?syn-25a6b1a6=1>its newly-hired associates with 90 days' pay, you might feel confused.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
This is what appears to have occurred at Weil, Gotshal & Manges, the law firm which handled Lehman's bankruptcy <https://edition.cnn.com/2026/10/28/business/weil-gotshal-and-manges-winds-down-operations>, but which is suddenly winding down after experiencing its own Lehman moment following the departure of key staff. </news/michael-aiello>
Last week, Weil Gotshal ingested 150+ new legal associates globally and put them through a week of 'new associate orientation' which it said was intended to "build and develop relationships, and learn more about the values that make Weil unique."
This week, in a now-deleted post across multiple social media platforms, the firm declared its deep commitment to young employees and celebrated sessions where "partners and associates spoke candidly about the relationships that have helped them grow throughout their careers."
One day later, the firm was revealed to be winding down. "That "deep commitment" to developing their futures went less than 24 hours," observed one person commenting on the post. The Financial Times <https://www.ft.com/content/98dfc71b-19eb-4194-8c6a-bb6d9b463074?syn-25a6b1a6=1> said there were tears among Weil Gotshal partners yesterday as they learned the firm is to be dissolved after 95 years.
Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-29/paul-weiss-simpson-race-to-hire-weil-lawyers-after-collapse> said rival law firms like Gibson Dunn, Simpson Thacher, Paul Weiss and Sullivan & Cromwell are rushing to hire Weil Gotshal's displaced staff. Unexpectedly Palantir has also thrown its hat into the ring, with CFO David Glazer pitching on LinkedIn for Weil's unwanted summer associates to get "a real summer job (with way less lunches) but way more fun."
In the meantime, Weil Gotshal's post (above) survives as a memory of what might have been. Comments suggested that it should be deleted. A previous post last week welcoming the new associates and promising them an opportunity to "learn more about the values that make Weil unique," is described in comments as having "aged like milk."
Last year, Sunny Singh, co-chair of Weil's restructuring department and a member of the management committee, sent a now viral email <https://x.com/eastsidedav/status/2115579518500864491?a=IJA7QqRnJho-d1_AyEM&s=20>relating to the First Brands bankruptcy. Manny Grillo at rival firm Orrick asked Singh (who was working for First Brands) whether First Brands received $1.9bn in factoring funds and how much was in segregated accounts to cover those funds. Singh responded, "“# 1 — We don’t know #2 — $0.” Maybe Orrick will now employ him.

item.title: Some new macro guys left Citadel and ExodusPoint in London
item.description:
In these days of hard times </news/hedge-funds-hired-too-many-morons-and-other-unpopular-opinions-as-the-industry-pukes-p-ms> for macro portfolio managers (PMs) and hard talk of 100 people leaving or losing </news/london-s-macro-hedge-fund-pain-as-up-to-100-people-are-out-everyone-has-blown-up>their jobs in London alone, it's unsurprising that PMs are leaving funds.
Not all the leavers across the industry have left involuntarily. Some are having a rest. Some have other plans. But many have gone.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Recent departures from Citadel's registered London entity include: Avi Tullu, a senior macro volatility portfolio manager who joined from Pimco in September 2025 and left again in September 2026; and Simon Roach, a former head of EMEA rates trading at Merrill Lynch, who left in early October after a long stint that began over a decade ago. Citadel declined to comment. The exits were previously reported by With Intelligence.
At ExodusPoint, macro departures from the registered London entity include other recent joiners. Senior macro analyst Soham Sengupta came in December 2025 and left in October 2026 according to the FCA Register. Rupert Guest, an FX trader from Barclays, joined in January 2025 and left again earlier this month. Jim McKeever, who joined from Caxton in 2024, left too. ExodusPoint declined to comment.
Amid the departures, new people arrived. As we reported </news/one-of-hsbc-s-top-fx-traders-escaped-to-citadel>earlier this month, Vineet Mudgil, an FX trader at HSBC in London, just escaped to Citadel after nearly 20 years with the bank. Juniors Emaad Alvi and Max Dykes also joined Citadel's macro team from Tudor and RBC respectively. In New York, Citadel plucked Pedro Goldbaum </news/citadel-hired-deutsche-bank-s-ex-citi-big-rates-guy>from Deutsche Bank.
One senior macro trader and former hedge fund PM who's been sitting out of the market, watching from the sidelines, observed that these are fine times for someone like him. "Banks have very few macro people left and funds need to hire," he said.

item.title: The best-paid AI specialists might work in banks, not hedge funds
item.description:
How well could working with AI pay if you are in London? Very well – $2m per head if you’re at OpenAI </news/open-ai-outpaid-quant-trading-firms-in-london-last-year-offering-2m-per-head-including-stock>, for example. But how well does working with AI pay outside of the frontier labs?
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/signup>✍️
A recent salary survey from recruitment firm Octavius Finance suggested that it is nowhere near that, perhaps predictably. It is London, after all.
Starting pay for an “Agentic AI Investment Analyst” varies between £35k ($47k) and £70k ($94k) depending on if you work at a consultancy/fintech </news/how-ai-is-changing-careers-in-fintech>, bank, or hedge fund </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job>, according to Octavius Finance. The highest salaries are at banks, where they range between £60k ($80k) and £70k ($94k), and also comes with a 10% to 20% bonus. Bonuses at hedge funds can be higher, although base salaries start lower.
For slightly more experienced AI analysts – those with 2 to 4 years of experience – salaries are highest at banks, where Octavius Finance says they are between £70k ($94k) and £85k ($114k), and at hedge funds, where they are between £60k ($80k) and £80k ($107k). They are lowest at consultancies and fintechs, where the range is just £45k ($60k) to £55k ($74k).
Bonuses, however, complicate things. For “senior” AI analysts at banks, Octavius Finance says these can be between 15% and 20% of salary, while at hedge funds, these can be 30% of salary upwards. At consultancies/fintechs, they are just 5% to 10% of salary.
Octavius Finance notes that there isn’t salary data for more senior roles than the above “because this is a new role with insufficient longer-tenure salary data,” amusingly. Who knows what these roles will offer in a few years, or if they will even exist at all then.
Either way, the pay isn’t high. A cursory look at job openings at Anthropic or OpenAI in San Francisco, where the firms are legally required to disclose compensation, rarely shows salaries below $200k, no matter the job title or level of experience. Those aren’t exactly like-for-like; Octavius Finance notes that the roles above refer to “applying and evaluating agents in investment research, rather than engineering the underlying AI infrastructure.”

item.title: Morning Coffee: How to make $1m talking about financial services on LinkedIn. Citi's head of London is leaving
item.description:
Many are the people who want to work in investment banks, </news/what-is-an-investment-bank>electronic trading </news/hft-pay-london> firms and hedge funds </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job>. Few are the people who actually do. If you have the good fortune to be in the latter category, the Financial Times <https://www.ft.com/content/4303c519-5e3b-4eeb-9871-d6a2845ac564?syn-25a6b1a6=1>suggests a new way of earning $50k a week has presented itself: becoming an influencer on LinkedIn.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
LinkedIn influencers are nothing new and have long been ridiculed on sites like Reddit <https://www.reddit.com/r/LinkedInLunatics/> for the vapidity of their niche. But times are changing and the FT has found people who say that LinkedIn has shifted its algorithm “from a feed that historically was all about your network and is [now] increasingly about the topics you’re interested in”. This apparently means that the site is now like "YouTube in the early 2010s, TikTok in 2018" and that brands will pay €50,000-€250,000 ($56k-$280k) sponsoring videos featuring trusted people. These brands include AI tools and customer relations platforms. These people include a marketing advisor at FedEx sharing career tips, and a software engineer at Airbnb, one of whom claims to have a “low seven-figure business by revenues”.
Sounds great, except banks aren't keen on people putting themselves out there on social media while still employed and the world is littered with people purporting to be other than they are </news/juliet-mackay-notbadjuju>, suddenly pulling their accounts after being found out </news/junior-banker-at-rbc-complains-of-3-hours-sleep-on-tik-tok-attracts-attention-of-hr>, or making themselves into an influencer and then finding it's hard to get employed. Such things are better left to retirement, or to Jon Gray, </news/jon-gray-blackstone>president of Blackstone, who probably doesn't need the sponsorship anyway.
Separately, Tiina Lee, Citi's chief executive officer in the UK is leaving the sort of regulated 'coupon-cutting' job </news/career-advice-banking> that pays a lot and can make you richer than a LinkedIn influencer if you keep your head down and all goes well.
The Banker <https://www.thebanker.com/content/401857c0-e4f3-498e-b7ce-99cd7ccf73cb> reports that Lee stepped down after three years. She is doing so around one week after saying <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-20/citi-committed-to-uk-even-if-bank-surcharge-raised-uk-ceo-says>that Citi is committed to the UK even if the British government increases the surcharge on banks, which has now happened.
Last year, Lee described </news/tiina-lee-citi-london> her high pressure childhood as the child of immigrant parents in Hampstead and said she was overseeing the construction of Citi's new London office with a winter garden.
As the official regulatory 'SMF1 Chief Executive' for Citi's London entity, Lee was personally accountable to regulators, and could have faced unlimited fines if found responsible for failings, or even prison in the event of a reckless decision that caused the bank to fail. There is no suggestion that this was a factor in her decision making. Now that the winter garden is open, maybe she decided there are better places to hang out.
Meanwhile...
There were tears as the chairman of Weil Gotshal revealed that the firm had exhausted its options and could be dissolved but now senior people at the law firm are being plagued by a "feeding frenzy" of recruiters. Young people are being paid for 90 days. (FT) < https://www.ft.com/content/98dfc71b-19eb-4194-8c6a-bb6d9b463074?syn-25a6b1a6=1>
JPMorgan will pay additional taxes of between £100m and £150m as a result of the corporation tax surcharge hike announced by John Healey in his budget. (Sky) <https://news.sky.com/story/jpmorgan-chase-faces-100m-plus-tax-bill-from-healey-raid-13604869>
ING is cutting 400 jobs in its wholesale banking unit. It is deploying AI “not only to save on costs, also to be able to enlarge the scalability of the growth.”(WSJ) <https://www.wsj.com/business/earnings/ing-launches-buyback-but-flags-job-cuts-and-unit-restructuring-b19efaf1>
Marshall Wace will now have to disclose the emails its executives Anthony Clake and Alan Hofmeyr sent when they were recruiting credit portfolio manager Daniel Shatz from Citadel. </news/citadel-marshall-wace>(Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-29/citadel-can-subpoena-top-marshall-wace-executives-judge-rules>
Carlos Fernandez-Aller, co-head of global fixed income, currencies and commodities macro trading at Bank of America, says: “The market is very fragile — any small mishap can cause a continuation of the unwinds that we saw. We are running a relatively small amount of risk.” (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-29/bofa-macro-traders-avoid-big-bets-after-volatile-market-shakeout>
Leopold Aschenbrenner of Situational Awareness is inviting people to invest alongside him in neocloud startup FluidStack. It's raised $830m so far. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-29/situational-awareness-pitches-investors-on-fluidstack-fundraise?srnd=homepage-uk>
32-year-old Australian Josh Payne wants to IPO his AI data centre business NScale for $30bn. “He’s a tremendous dealmaker,” says an early investor. Bloomberg says Payne's previous career includes an unprofitable Bitcoin mining operation, a failed special purpose acquisition vehicle and some investment firms with no identifiable portfolio or track record. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/features/2026-10-29/nscale-s-unproven-ceo-braves-ai-turmoil-in-bid-for-30-billion-neocloud-ipo>
Absa's got a new Dubai office. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-29/absa-opens-dubai-office-as-lender-accelerates-expansion-plan>

item.title: Barclays’ new head of AI has already attracted an anonymous complaint
item.description:
As we reported last week </news/barclays-ai-job-cuts>, Barclays has got itself a new chief AI officer in the form of Anita Tanna.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Tanna was appointed last Friday and declared on LinkedIn that she was "excited" and that she would be "focused on accelerating adoption [of AI] across the group." Her elevation came as Barclays said it would be cutting 5,000 jobs with the help of AI, with 60% of the cuts coming from support functions. <https://www.ft.com/content/e83591cd-13d4-4358-aee9-c500930bfd36?syn-25a6b1a6=1> Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-23/barclays-vows-to-redeploy-staff-to-offset-pain-of-5-000-job-cuts>reported that the bank plans to redeploy staff where possible but there is skepticism about such promises. "Frankly the whole relocation carrot is a joke, fake and soul crushing," wrote someone on our previous article </news/barclays-ai-job-cuts>last week.
In the circumstances, it's perhaps unsurprising that Tanna's appointment hasn't been universally welcomed. However, an anonymous letter from people purporting to be Barclays insiders claims that the issues with Tanna go beyond the fact that Barclays' AI push is associated with thousands of job cuts. The letter questions whether someone with "deep domain expertise" in "computer science or machine learning architecture" should have got the job and whether the appointment went through a competitive recruitment process. Tanna, who spent much of her career in equity sales at Barclays and Citi, was chief of staff to Barclays CEO C.S. Venkatakrishnan from January 2024.
"Elevating an executive without technical credentials to spearhead this transition proves that the announced restructuring is not an objective technological evolution," says the letter, which is addressed to Barclays' chairman and copied in to the co-COO.
The letter offers little to support its claims. It's not unusual for CEOs to promote a trusted colleague. Nor is it unusual for AI heads to have non-technical backgrounds. In its paper <https://www.fca.org.uk/publications/good-poor-practice/ai-financial-services#lf-chapter-id-governance-and-accountability-senior-management-function-smf-and-reasonable-steps>on good practice for AI in financial services last week, the FCA said specifically that it doesn't "expect senior managers to be technical specialists."
The FCA said senior managers responsible for AI do need to "take reasonable steps to understand the risks arising from AI use within their area of responsibility, and obtain appropriate information and expertise where necessary."
Barclays declined to comment and Tanna didn't respond to a request to comment.
The bank is already in the process of making its 5,000 job cuts, with developers and employees in locations like Northampton </news/barclays-ai-job-cuts> particularly affected.

item.title: A top JPMorgan trader asked to move from London to Dubai. Some are moving the other way
item.description:
If you're a trader and you're moving from London to the UAE, you are probably joining a hedge fund. Hedge funds have embraced the Emirates with enthusiasm </news/traders-london-to-dubai-abu-dhabi-hedge-funds>. Even Jain Global </news/jain-global>is getting an office there. <https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/jain-global-plans-dubai-office-amid-middle-east-hedge-fund-rush-48d89756>
Moving to the Emirates is less easy if you're at a bank. Banks are typically less willing to move staff internally to the oasis of low taxation. But it does happen.
It happened at JPMorgan, where we understand that Duncan Barclay, a top EuroStoxx trader in London wanted to move to Dubai. JPMorgan obliged and Barclay is thought to have arrived there recently. JPMorgan declined to comment on his relocation.
Barclay's migration follows that of various other London traders who've left banks for hedge funds in the Emirates ever since war in the Middle East broke out in February. Some, like Daniel Dangoor, who left Goldman Sachs in London for ExodusPoint in Dubai in June, have since left again.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Yesterday, the British government updated its travel advice <https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/united-arab-emirates> for the Middle East, to caution that, "The context in the Middle East remains deeply unpredictable and the risk of sudden escalation is high," and that, "British nationals in, or planning to travel through, the Middle East should be prepared for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions."
Finance professionals in the Middle East are nonetheless adamant that life there is better. "I lived in the UK for two decades and I loved it," one senior trader tells us. "But the taxes in the UK are too much. I'm not getting any younger and I don't have many years left in which to cash in."
Despite many such sentiments, some senior traders are choosing London over other locations. Citadel's London office, for example, recently hired David Caulfield, an equities portfolio manager from Millennium in Dubai. It also hired Raphael Magrath, who was last seen trading agricultural commodities for a fund in Rio de Janeiro.
One London salesperson told us he would never move to Dubai. "Whenever I visit clients in Dubai they are so desperate for you to visit them," he said. "You read between the lines – you can tell they're lonely. Some people love it, but I wouldn’t want to go two months at a time without seeing my wife and kids”

item.title: A rates sales guy nurtured by Deutsche Bank is no longer there
item.description:
Rates sales can be a lucrative business. Just ask Puni Raja at Barclays </news/punitha-raja-barclays>or Nohshad Shah and Frank Flight, </news/citadel-securities-is-making-its-ex-goldman-sachs-macro-vp-famous> who left Goldman Sachs and are both now at Citadel Securities in London.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Deutsche Bank had an up-and-coming hedge fund rates sales guy whom it promoted to vice president in February. Now it doesn't. Alexander Akinbile is understood to have left the German bank in recent weeks, possibly for a fund. He spent five years there after joining as an intern in 2020.
Akinbile didn't respond to a request to comment for this article. Deutsche Bank declined to comment.
We presume that Deutsche Bank wanted to keep Akinbile. It nurtured him for five long years. He was not senior, but is thought to have been pretty good.
